title: Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
authors: Pashler et al.; Institute of Education Sciences
summary: The practice guide recommends spacing, alternating worked solutions with practice, combining graphics and words, and connecting concrete and abstract representations.
decision: Include revisits, fading assistance, and explicit links among representations.
limitation: Recommendations are not a globally optimal mathematics sequence; evidence levels differ by recommendation.
asset_policy: Reference metadata only in the public repository. Full text is held externally with provenance and access rights.

title: ACT-R cognitive architecture
authors: ACT-R Research Group, Carnegie Mellon University
summary: ACT-R distinguishes declarative and procedural memory, with limited buffers mediating access to modules. Model assumptions are tested against human accuracy and timing.
decision: Keep memory storage separate from the active buffer and make retrieval assumptions inspectable.
limitation: Our trace-decay simulator is inspired by these distinctions; it is not an ACT-R implementation or a validated human model.
asset_policy: Reference metadata only in the public repository. Full text is held externally with provenance and access rights.

title: Modeling individual differences in working memory performance: a source activation account
summary: The paper models differences in working memory performance through activation within a cognitive architecture.
decision: Vary memory and retrieval parameters across simulated learner profiles instead of assigning one universal capacity.
limitation: A fitted model in a particular task does not establish an appropriate capacity for advanced mathematics.

title: Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning
summary: The paper relates schema acquisition and novice problem solving to cognitive processing demands and includes a computational account and experiments.
decision: Offer worked examples and manageable subgoals before removing assistance.
limitation: Do not infer that discovery or independent problem solving is always harmful; expertise and task design matter.

title: Self-Explanations: How Students Study and Use Examples in Learning to Solve Problems
authors: Chi, Bassok, Lewis, Reimann, and Glaser
summary: Talk-aloud work on mechanics examples examines the relationship between self-explanations, monitoring, and later problem solving. The linked technical report precedes the journal article.
decision: Ask learners why a step works; distinguish their spoken account from an automatically inferred cognitive process.
limitation: This is not evidence that a speech transcript reveals all thought or that verbal fluency measures mastery.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics

decision: Track assistance, avoid equating supported success with learning, and include later unassisted assessments.
limitation: One educational setting and model configuration do not establish effects for every tutor, age, or subject.
